Sup guys, I don’t usually post stuff like this. I’m not the type who likes to share my opinions on social media... most of the time I just scroll, laugh at memes, and move on. But honestly, what’s happening in our country right now feels too alarming to just ignore. For the first time, I feel like I need to use this space to speak up, even just as a small voice, to share what’s really going on.

Lately, I’ve been thinking about how much budget is being poured into flood control projects here in the Philippines. Every year, big amounts are set aside to address flooding, which we all know is a huge problem during typhoon season. But when we look around, the reality doesn’t seem to match what’s promised. There are what people call “ghost projects.” Those that are listed on paper and supposedly completed, but in reality, there’s nothing there or the work is so poorly done it barely helps. It’s painful to know that while the money is there, the solutions often aren’t.

I’m thankful that I live in a place where flooding doesn’t really affect me directly. I know that’s a privilege, and I don’t take it for granted. But I also can’t ignore the fact that many Filipinos don’t have the same luck. For them, floods mean lost homes, destroyed crops, and endless struggles to rebuild again and again. And knowing that so much of this suffering could have been prevented if the funds were used properly. It really makes you stop and think.

Of course, I don’t want this to sound like I’m saying everything is hopeless. I still believe there are good people in government, hardworking engineers, and communities trying to do the right thing. It’s just that corruption and inefficiency often overshadow the good, leaving people discouraged. That’s why I wanted to write this post... not as a rant, but as a reminder. A reminder that accountability matters, that transparency matters, and that patience matters too. Change takes time, but it starts with awareness and voices, even small ones like this.

So if you’ve read this far, thank you. This is me stepping out of my comfort zone to share something I normally wouldn’t post. I hope this can serve as a little voice in the middle of the noise. A voice that still believes there is hope, but also knows we need to be patient. At the end of the day, this is our country. And even if it’s just through simple reminders like this, we can keep pushing for a future where resources are used honestly, and where people don’t have to live in fear every time the rains come.
